html:
The Georgian alphabet is the script of the Georgian language, first seen in inscriptions of the 400s. The oldest are from the 430s at a Georgian monastery near Bethlehem and the 490s at the Bolnisi Sioni church south of Tbilisi.

Georgian tradition credits a king of the 200s BCE, but most scholars link it to the spread of Christianity, like the Armenian alphabet at about the same time, so that scripture and liturgy could be written in Georgian. Three forms developed over time: the rounded asomtavruli, the angular nuskhuri of church books, and mkhedruli, the form used today. Mkhedruli has 33 letters, with no capitals. It carried a rich literature, including The Knight in the Panther's Skin. In 2016 UNESCO listed the three scripts as living heritage of Georgia.
